4. Canonical Cargo Receptor Activity: Simultaneous Binding of Cargo and COPII Coat (Pagant et al., 2015)
The most mechanistically rigorous evidence came from Pagant et al. (2015, Current Biology), using targeted mutagenesis:

Conserved residues in the second transmembrane domain of Erv14 were identified that mediate interaction with a subset of Erv14 clients. [PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4334704/)
Interaction of Erv14 with a novel cargo-binding surface on Sec24 is necessary for efficient trafficking of all of its clients. [PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4334704/)
Some Erv14 clients also directly engage an adjacent cargo-binding domain of Sec24, suggesting a novel mode of dual interaction between cargo and coat. [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982214015711)
